q: Who first excavated Harappa in 1921?
e: Daya Ram Sahni excavated Harappa in 1921; R. D. Banerji excavated Mohenjo-daro in 1922.

q: The 'Great Bath' of the Indus Valley Civilisation was found at:
e: The Great Bath is the best-known structure found at Mohenjo-daro.

q: Which Harappan site is famous for its dockyard?
e: Lothal in Gujarat had a dockyard, showing sea trade.

q: Which is the oldest of the four Vedas?
e: The Rigveda is the oldest Veda and a collection of hymns.

q: Gautama Buddha was born at:
e: Buddha was born at Lumbini, in present-day Nepal.

q: Where did Gautama Buddha deliver his first sermon?
e: The first sermon at Sarnath is called Dharmachakra Pravartana.

q: Who was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism?
e: Vardhamana Mahavira was the 24th Tirthankara; Parshvanatha was the 23rd.

q: Who founded the Maurya Empire?
e: Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire with the help of Chanakya.

q: Ashoka adopted Buddhism after which war?
e: The bloodshed of the Kalinga War led Ashoka to adopt Buddhism and Dhamma.

q: The 'Arthashastra' is attributed to:
e: Kautilya (Chanakya) is credited with the Arthashastra, a text on statecraft.

q: 'Indica', an account of Mauryan India, was written by:
e: Megasthenes, a Greek envoy at Chandragupta Maurya's court, wrote Indica.

q: Which ruler is called the 'Napoleon of India' because of his conquests?
e: Historian V. A. Smith called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India'.

q: The 'Tripitakas' are sacred texts of which religion?
e: The Tripitaka (three baskets) is the Buddhist canon.

q: The Gayatri Mantra is found in which Veda?
e: The Gayatri Mantra, addressed to Savitr, is in the third Mandala of the Rigveda.

q: Which Chinese pilgrim visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II?
e: Fa-Hien came to India in the early 5th century during Chandragupta II's rule.

q: Hiuen Tsang visited India during the reign of:
e: Hiuen Tsang stayed in India in the 7th century, in Harsha's time.

q: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held under the patronage of:
e: The Fourth Council was held in Kashmir under Kushan king Kanishka.

q: What was the capital of the Kushan ruler Kanishka?
e: Purushapura (modern Peshawar) was Kanishka's capital.

q: The Allahabad Pillar inscription (Prayag Prashasti) composed by Harisena praises:
e: Court poet Harisena composed it to describe Samudragupta's conquests.

q: The poet Kalidasa is traditionally associated with the court of:
e: Kalidasa is regarded as one of the 'Navaratnas' of Chandragupta II Vikramaditya.

q: Sangam literature was composed in which language?
e: Sangam literature is the earliest Tamil literature.

q: Who first deciphered the Brahmi script of Ashoka's inscriptions in 1837?
e: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi, allowing Ashoka's edicts to be read.

q: Which statement about the script of the Harappan civilisation is correct?
o: It was deciphered by James Prinsep
It is the same as the Brahmi script
It was written in Greek letters
It has not been deciphered yet
e: The Indus script is still undeciphered, so much about the civilisation is unknown.

q: Megasthenes came to India as the ambassador of:
e: Seleucus Nicator sent Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.

q: Alexander fought the Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum) in 326 BC against:
e: King Porus fought Alexander on the banks of the Hydaspes (Jhelum).

q: Where did Mahavira attain nirvana (death)?
e: Mahavira died at Pavapuri (Pawapuri) near Rajgir in Bihar.

q: The list of sixteen Mahajanapadas is found in which Buddhist text?
e: The Anguttara Nikaya lists the 16 Mahajanapadas such as Magadha, Kosala and Avanti.

q: Chalukya king Pulakeshin II defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of which river?
e: The Aihole inscription records Pulakeshin II stopping Harsha at the Narmada.

q: The Iron Pillar at Mehrauli (Delhi) bears an inscription of a king named Chandra, generally identified with:
e: The rust-resistant Iron Pillar is a Gupta-period work linked to Chandragupta II.

q: Who wrote the Sanskrit play 'Mudrarakshasa'?
e: Vishakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa tells how Chanakya helped Chandragupta Maurya win power.
